orch.hintSection: [ha-orchestrator plugin context] You are equipped with the subagent orchestration tool orchestrate (fanout parallel / pipeline staged / supervisor review-merge). When the task meets ANY of the following, call orchestrate directly and automatically in the first turn — no explicit user request needed, and do not serially handle each item yourself (especially for "read/understand a large project or codebase", do not start with sequential read/glob browsing): (1) it decomposes into 2+ independent subtasks (e.g. reading/understanding a large project or codebase, multi-file research, batch review, comparing options, multi-repo checks); (2) it needs staged progress (e.g. requirements → design → implementation plan); (3) it needs a senior review gate (e.g. code review, design review, QA). Decompose the goal into tasks yourself (each task with a clear, self-contained prompt); even if you do not know the project yet, roughly split tasks by module/directory/doc/code area and let subagents read in parallel before you summarize; this is the unified orchestration entry point, preferred over one-by-one dispatch with subagent/subagent_fork; for custom subagents, query the roster (name/provider/description) via the list-subagents tool first.
orch.mergeDefault: Review all subtask outputs and merge them into one accurate, complete, deduplicated conclusion; note anything still missing or uncertain.
orch.rosterHead: Available custom subagents (referenced by name via tasks[].agent or the top-level agent):
orch.rosterHint: Query the available custom subagent list (name/provider/description) via the list-subagents tool.
orch.stageRetryHint: Retries per failed pipeline stage (0 = fail-fast, stop later stages)
orch.title: Subagent Orchestration
orch.toolAgentField: Each task may name a custom subagent via the agent field; the top-level agent sets the default subagent; supervisorAgent names the supervisor;
orch.toolAutoUse: Auto-call this tool without waiting for an explicit user request, and do not handle items serially yourself, when the task meets ANY of: it can be split into 2+ independent subtasks (including reading/understanding a large project or codebase, multi-file research, batch review, comparing options, multi-repo checks); it needs staged pipeline progress; or it needs a senior review gate. For "read/understand a large project" tasks, call this tool in the first turn to split the work into parallel subtasks instead of browsing sequentially with read/glob; even if you do not know the project yet, roughly split tasks by module/directory/doc/code area and let subagents read in parallel before you summarize. This is the unified orchestration entry point; do not manually fan out with subagent/subagent_fork one by one.
orch.toolDefault: Uses the default model when unspecified.
orch.toolFanout: fanout: run tasks in parallel across subagents and summarize;
orch.toolListSubagents: List the currently available custom subagents (name / provider / model / description). Subagents are referenced by name in orchestrate (tasks[].agent, top-level agent, supervisorAgent) — query this list first to pick one.
orch.toolPipeline: pipeline: run sequentially, each task output feeding the next task as input context;
orch.toolSupervisor: supervisor: run all tasks in parallel first, then a supervisor subagent reviews and merges per mergeInstructions.
orch.toolYouAre: You are the orchestrator: break the goal into tasks yourself (each task has a clear, self-contained prompt).
orch.usageHowto: The model calls orchestrate automatically on tasks suited to parallel decomposition (e.g. reading a large project, multi-file research), multi-stage work, or review.
